topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: A benchmark compares selected alternatives; a profiler helps discover where a real workload spends resources. Begin with a representative task and a correctness result, then use samples or counters to investigate a suspected bottleneck. Harbor’s lookup workload deliberately separates linear scanning from indexed lookup so the call graph has a meaningful architectural question behind it.

topics.title: 13.1.1 Measuring Function-Level CPU Time
topics.summary: A sampling profiler periodically records where execution is observed. A function receiving many samples is a candidate for investigation, not automatic proof that its source is inefficient. It may be called frequently because of an upstream design choice, or it may be doing necessary work for a dominant workload.

topics.title: 13.1.2 Inspecting Call Graphs
topics.summary: A call graph connects expensive work to its callers. Inclusive cost includes descendants; exclusive cost refers to the function itself under the tool’s model. Optimized inlining and tail calls can change the apparent structure, so retain symbols and understand the profiler’s unwinding method.

blocks.text: Code or command

blocks.text:
g++ -O2 -g workload.cpp -o workload
perf record -g -- ./workload
perf report --stdio --sort comm,dso,symbol | head -40

topics.title: 13.2.1 Measuring Cache Misses
topics.summary: Hardware counters expose selected microarchitectural events, subject to processor support and operating-system permissions. A cache-miss count can help explain a memory-access pattern, but event names and meanings vary by processor. Multiplexed measurements may be scaled estimates rather than simultaneous exact counts.

topics.title: 13.2.2 Measuring Branch Behavior
topics.summary: Branch-related events can reveal difficult-to-predict control flow, but source-level if statements do not map one-to-one to branch instructions. Compilers can use conditional moves, vector masks, or algebraic transformations. Inspect generated code before attributing a counter change to a particular line.

topics.title: Solution and review notes
topics.summary: A separate mode makes attribution clearer, but it must process the same query bytes and report the same hit count. Linear search can terminate early on present keys, while absent keys scan the entire sequence. That difference explains why a distribution change affects its work even before considering hardware counters.
